items.title: Media practitioners welcome return of 300-litre Budi95 monthly quota
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Association of Malaysian Media Clubs (GKMM) has welcomed the government's decision to restore the basic quota under the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme from 200 litres to 300 litres a month from Sept 1, describing it as a relief for media practitioners. GKMM president Mohd Fauzi Ishak said the decision would particularly benefit media practitioners working in the states, who previously faced difficulties and had to bear higher monthly expenses for RON95. He said GKMM also hoped companies and media agencies nationwide would consider introducing new incentives or allowances for their media practitioners, in view of the rising costs involved in carrying out their duties.

items.title: Nepal tragedy: Missing trekker's son stays calm while awaiting news of father
items.summary: The 24-year-old engineer said he was satisfied with the comprehensive efforts by the ministries involved in managing the crisis. His father, Shabuddin Mun, is among the Malaysians reported missing during a trekking expedition using a four-wheel-drive vehicle with the Team Loe group. On today's briefing session at Wisma Putra, Firas said it served as a good platform for coordinating information and ensuring all family members received accurate updates.

items.title: Number of uncontactable Malaysians remains at 36 in China, 55 in Nepal - Foreign Ministry
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The number of Malaysians reported uncontactable remains at 36 in China and 55 in Nepal, despite earlier reports that three Malaysians were among foreigners unaccounted for following a mudslide at Gyirong Port in Xizang, China. "The ministry confirms that these three Malaysians are already included in the 36 Malaysians currently reported as uncontactable in China and do not represent additional cases. "As such, the current figures remain at 36 Malaysians (in China) and 55 Malaysians (in Nepal).

items.title: Family returns from weddings to find home destroyed by fire
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A family who had left their home in Kampung Pasir Kota for less than an hour to attend two wedding ceremonies returned to find their wooden house razed by fire today. Neighbour Che Ibrahim Che Ahmad, 63, said the house belonged to a woman known as 'Mak Nik', in her 70s, who lived alone. "I rushed out of my house and saw flames coming from Mak Nik's home.

items.title: 'Some fatalities' in ferry capsize off Northern Cyprus
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Some people died when a ferry capsized off Northern Cyprus on Sunday, the head of the local government said, without giving a precise toll. "There are some fatalities," Unal Ustel, prime minister of the self-proclaimed Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), said, according to Turkiye's state news agency Anadolu. The capsize occurred shortly after the ferry departed from the Northern Cyprus port of Kyrenia headed for the Turkish port of Tasucu.

items.title: Sarawak prepares for possible Disaster Emergency if haze reaches critical level
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak is ready to declare a Disaster Emergency if the haze situation, which saw three areas record hazardous air quality readings, reaches a critical level, reports said. According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), three air quality monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded hazardous API readings as of 8pm today. Eight areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings ranging from 152 to 198.

items.title: Peka urges public inquiry before Pahang forest reserves are degazetted
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail has been urged to hold a public inquiry before permanent reserved forests are degazetted, with Pertubuhan Pelindung Khazanah Alam Malaysia (Peka) calling for greater scrutiny of such decisions. "If Pahang's process is truly transparent, responsible and 'working well', then hold a public inquiry," he said. "A public inquiry is not an attack on the state government's powers.

items.title: Smart team on standby, awaits Nepalese govt nod for SAR assistance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Special Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) is on standby for deployment to Nepal to assist search and rescue (SAR) operations following devastating floods in the country. However, the agency said the deployment would remain subject to the Nepalese government's requirements and official decision to accept Malaysia's assistance. Meanwhile, Smart team commander Manaf Mat Isa, when met by reporters at Smart headquarters, said the team had made the necessary preparations for a possible deployment.

items.title: Iceland votes 'No' to resuming EU talks
items.summary: REYKJAVIK: Iceland voted 'No' to resuming membership negotiations with the European Union, final referendum results showed Sunday, dealing a heavy blow to Brussels which had been keen to welcome a new wealthy member. In a vote held Saturday, 52.8 percent of Icelanders rejected the resumption of EU entry talks suspended 13 years ago, while 47.2 percent voted 'Yes', according to the official tally published by RUV, the public broadcaster. The result will also likely bury the EU question in Iceland until at least 2028.

items.title: Nepal floods: Family pleads with govt to bring missing Malaysians home, whatever their condition
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: After nearly five days of anxious waiting, the family of 65-year-old N. Kalaiselvi, who remains uncontactable in Nepal, is urging the government to bring the missing Malaysians home, regardless of their condition. Her daughter, Kritikaa Joyce De Brito, said the family appreciated the Malaysian government's efforts to coordinate the search and rescue mission, but acknowledged that their hopes were fading after nearly five days without contact. She said that even if rescue teams successfully reached the affected area, the chances of finding the missing Malaysians alive could be slim given the conditions there.

items.title: 69 years on: What does Merdeka mean to Malaysians? [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Unity, freedom of choice and preserving the peace built by earlier generations were among the views shared by Malaysians from two generations ahead of the country's 69th National Day. The New Straits Times brought together five Malaysians from the Merdeka and Gen Z generations to share their views on freedom, their experiences of Malaysia and their hopes for the country. O'Hara said the freedom she valued most was the freedom of choice.

items.title: Over 1.1 million MSMEs to benefit from higher e-Invoice exemption threshold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 1.1 million micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) will be exempted from implementing e-Invoicing following the government's decision to raise the implementation threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million. The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) said that with the higher threshold, MSMEs with annual income or sales of less than RM3 million would not be required to implement e-Invoicing. "This Madani government initiative reflects the government's concern in easing the compliance burden and costs incurred by MSMEs.

items.title: Russia says preparing 'massive strikes' on Ukraine's energy sector
items.summary: MOSCOW: Russia's defence ministry on Sunday said it was gearing up for large-scale attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure in a tit-for-tat response to strikes by Kyiv. "Russian forces have begun preparations for massive strikes against facilities in Ukraine's energy sector in response to the ongoing attacks by the Kyiv regime on civilian infrastructure and on Russia's oil and energy complex," it said on Telegram. Last winter, Moscow repeatedly hit Ukrainian power plants, devastating the country's energy sector and plunging millions of people into cold and darkness in sub-zero temperatures.

items.title: Survivors recount how Nepal landslides, floods swept away once-bustling bazaar
items.summary: NUWAKOT (Nepal): For Santosh Thapa, his family was lucky when a devastating mudslide hit Devighat in Nuwakot, central Nepal, as all his relatives managed to escape the disaster, leaving their belongings behind as mud gushed into the area. It was a narrow escape, Thapa said. Although he was in Kathmandu at the time, his relatives who were affected by the disaster told him what had happened, Xinhua reported.

items.title: Takiyuddin: PH-Bersatu cooperation talk signals political shift
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The possibility of Pakatan Harapan (PH) working with Bersatu in the upcoming Melaka state election is another indication that the two parties are moving towards political cooperation, said Perikatan Nasional (PN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan. Takiyuddin, who is also Pas secretary-general, said PH's openness to working with Bersatu, after previously cooperating with Umno, raised questions about the nature of the political relationship between the parties. Takiyuddin said the development could be seen as an admission by PH that it was prepared to establish political cooperation with Bersatu.

items.title: Families, friends cling to hope for three Malaysian climbers missing in Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The families and friends of three Malaysian climbers reported missing following a flash flood and landslide in the Nepal-Tibet border area last Wednesday are still hoping for good news about their safety. The three climbers are Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, 27, Muhammad Adib Haikal Awang Mansor, 27, and Muhammad Zaki Othman, 29, who were reported uncontactable while undertaking a climbing activity in the Langtang Valley. In a post on Threads, a friend of the three climbers appealed to the public to continue praying for their safety.

items.title: Manhunt in Switzerland after fatal rave shooting
items.summary: AARAU, Switzerland: Swiss police were on Sunday hunting gunmen who opened fire at a rave, killing one person and wounding five others, some of them seriously. According to local media, shots were fired before 3am (0100 GMT) near the Aarauer Rave, an annual techno party attended by some 3,500 people at the Aarau racetrack from Saturday afternoon to Sunday morning. They are suffering from injuries ranging from minor to serious," local police announced on X.

items.title: Restored Budi95 quota to provide relief, but enforcement must continue, says consumer groups
items.summary: The Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) said such a move would particularly benefit consumers with higher fuel consumption, while the government must ensure subsidised fuel reached genuine Malaysian users. Its chief executive officer Dr Saravanan Thambirajah said consumers with higher fuel consumption, particularly owners of diesel vehicles such as pickup trucks and jeeps, would benefit most from the increase. Saravanan said the government must ensure the subsidy reached genuine Malaysian users, warning that a higher quota would raise the stakes for enforcement.

items.title: MMA calls for clear timeline, accountability for RM1bil EMR investment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should set a clear implementation timeline, measurable milestones and accountability measures for the newly announced RM1 billion allocation for Electronic Medical Records (EMR) and connectivity across public healthcare facilities. Malaysian Medical Association president Datuk Dr R. Thirunavukarasu, however, welcomed the allocation, describing it as an important boost towards modernising the public healthcare system and enabling better connected care. He said these achievements reflected the work already being undertaken by teams driving the Health Ministry's digital health transformation, despite existing resource constraints.

items.title: SME groups approve of 3 govt initiatives announced by Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Small and medium enterprise groups have welcomed three government initiatives announced today, saying these would help ease pressures on SMEs, micro businesses and small traders. SME Association of Malaysia president Dr Chin Chee Seong said the measures were timely as businesses continued to grapple with rising operating costs and a challenging business environment. Chin said the initiatives would provide much-needed assistance to smaller businesses with limited financial and manpower resources.

items.title: Young Malaysians can get 3 months' free ILMUchat Pro from Merdeka Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians aged 18 to 30 can claim three months of free access to ILMUchat Pro from Merdeka Day after completing national artificial intelligence (AI) training under the AI Untuk Rakyat initiative. The programme, which targets 100,000 young Malaysians, is a collaboration between the Digital Ministry, YTL AI Labs and MyDigital Corporation, delivered through the Rakyat Digital platform. YTL AI Labs chief executive officer Foong Chee Mun said the company was proud to support the government's goal of making Malaysia a leading AI nation.

items.title: Serian records hazardous API of 436, followed by Samarahan and Kuching
items.summary: Of the 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide, none recorded good air quality, while 50 were in the moderate range and 18 recorded readings ranging from unhealthy to hazardous. Meanwhile, Labuan recorded an API reading of 153, while Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded 142 and Limbang, Sarawak, 130. In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda recorded an API reading of 110, while Taiping, Perak, recorded 106.

items.title: AI for Rakyat programme to equip 100,000 youths with AI tools
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Youths aged between 18 and 30 will be eligible for three months of free access to selected artificial intelligence (AI) tools after completing six modules under the new AI for Rakyat programme. "The six modules are AI Nation 2030: Madani Approach, Cybersafe for Rakyat, Generative AI, AI Safety, Agentic AI for All and Cloud for Rakyat. "Participants who successfully complete all six modules will receive three months of free access to selected AI applications and software.

items.title: Mat Sabu urges more Bumiputera farmers to go big in commercial agriculture
items.summary: SERDANG: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu wants more Bumiputera farmers to compete in large-scale agriculture, encouraged by the growing number of young people taking up farming full-time. "We hope the younger generation will take up agriculture full-time," he said at the launch of new pomelo and sweet potato varieties at Maha 2026 here today. Mohamad said Bumiputera farmers should compete with communities already established in commercial agriculture.

items.title: Langkawi ferry operators urge urgent dredging of Kuala Kedah, Kuala Perlis lanes
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: Langkawi ferry operators are appealing to the federal government to expedite dredging works in the shipping lanes at Kuala Kedah and Kuala Perlis, where silt deposits are affecting navigational safety. Ferry Line Ventures Sdn Bhd operations manager Lieutenant Commander (Retired) Norhafiz Abdul Wahid said increasingly shallow shipping lanes not only increased the risk to passenger ferry operations but could also cause schedule disruptions and travel delays. Norhafiz said comprehensive and periodic dredging works were needed to ensure the shipping routes remained safe, while allowing ferry operations to run smoothly and accommodate increased passenger numbers.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia's economic strength shines amid geopolitical uncertainty
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia's six per cent gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the second quarter of this year marks a new chapter in the country's journey towards greater progress and prosperity. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the achievement was particularly encouraging as it came amid an uncertain geopolitical environment, especially the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. No one.

items.title: Anwar: Economic growth benefits must be shared fairly among Malaysians
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government must ensure that the benefits of Malaysia's economic growth are shared fairly among all segments of society, regardless of race, religion, region or background, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the Madani government faced the challenge of balancing the needs of different groups, including the M40 and B40, Malay and Bumiputera communities, minorities, Sabah and Sarawak, as well as youths, women, persons with disabilities and workers in various sectors. Anwar also said the government must take into account the needs of young people, workers, women, farmers, fishermen, hawkers and gig workers.

items.title: Asyraf Wajdi, Dr Akmal to attend Pas Muktamar, says Takiyuddin
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Kelantan Umno leaders, including the state liaison chairman and division chiefs, have confirmed their attendance at the Pas muktamar. "The confirmed attendees are the Umno secretary-general and Umno leaders in Kelantan, including the state liaison chairman and division chiefs. "Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh will attend the Youth muktamar.

items.title: Communications Ministry to step up efforts to spread information on government assistance
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Communications Ministry will step up efforts to ensure Malaysians are better informed about government assistance, initiatives and achievements. Its minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the ministry would help communicate the various measures announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, including financial assistance and fuel subsidies, and ensure the information reached the public effectively. Fahmi said his ministry would also communicate other measures announced during the address, including the decision to raise the e-Invoice exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million.

items.title: Firefighter's brother to join Smart mission in Nepal to search for missing sibling
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The brother of Malaysian firefighter Mohd Fakhrul Munir, who remains uncontactable in Nepal, will join the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) mission to the country following the disaster in Rasuwa. Mohd Saiful Munir Mohd Isa, 46, said he would join the rescue mission as a member of the team while also hoping to obtain news on the whereabouts and condition of his 44-year-old younger brother, known as 'Loe'. Saiful said he hoped his presence in Nepal would enable him to contribute to the rescue mission while providing some relief to the family, which is still waiting for news of Mohd Fakhrul.
